'''Gareth W. Peters''' is an Australian [[wiktionary:endowed chair|endowed chair]] [[professor]] of [[actuarial science]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gareth Peters {{!}} UC Santa Barbara |url=https://www.pstat.ucsb.edu/people/gareth-peters |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=www.pstat.ucsb.edu |language=en}}</ref> and an [[Honorary title (academic)|honorary]] professor of statistics at [[University College London]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Emeritus & Honorary staff {{!}} University College London |url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/statistics/hidden/people/emeritus-honorary-staff |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=www.ucl.ac.uk |date=31 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref> As at 2024, he is also a member of the international advisory board of the [[Institute of Statistical Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Institute of Statistical Mathematics |url=https://www.ism.ac.jp/gaiyo-news/youran-e/2023en.pdf |access-date=2024-03-31}}</ref>

== Education ==
Peters has both a [[Bachelor of Engineering]] and [[Bachelor of Science]] with first class honors from the [[University of Melbourne]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae: Dr. Gareth W. Peters |url=https://web.maths.unsw.edu.au/~peterga/GWP/Gareth_Peters_Resume.pdf |access-date=2024-03-19 |website=web.maths.unsw.edu.au |language=en}}</ref> a [[Master of Science]] from the [[University of Cambridge]] and a [[PhD]] in Mathematics and Statistics from the [[University of New South Wales]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gareth W. Peters |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37409548900 |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=[[IEEE]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Before joining the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], Peters held academic positions at [[Heriot-Watt University]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Call for data standards to govern Edinburgh's data growth |url=https://www.scotsman.com/news/call-for-data-standards-to-govern-edinburghs-data-growth-199922 |access-date=2024-03-19 |website=www.scotsman.com |date=29 November 2018 |language=en}}</ref> [[University College London]] and [[University of New South Wales]].<ref name=":1" /> He has published over 150 peer-reviewed articles on risk and insurance modelling and 2 research text books on Operational Risk and Insurance. He has also been the editor and contributor to 3 edited text books on Monte Carlo methods and spatial statistics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gareth W. Peters {{!}} Risk.net |url=https://www.risk.net/author/gareth-w-peters |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=www.risk.net |date=27 October 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

== Research work ==
 [[Gareth W. Peters]] is a researcher primarily in time series modelling and econometrics, quantitative risk, actuarial science and insurance. Peters' research shows that [[mortality rates]] have [[heteroscedastic]] behaviour and incorporating heteroscedasticity and [[stochastic volatility]] in the estimation of [[life tables]] markedly improves model fit despite an increase of model complexity.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fung |first1=Man Chung |last2=Peters |first2=Gareth W. |last3=Shevchenko |first3=Pavel V. |date=2017 |title=A unified approach to mortality modelling using state-space framework: characterisation, identification, estimation and forecasting |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/annals-of-actuarial-science/article/unified-approach-to-mortality-modelling-using-statespace-framework-characterisation-identification-estimation-and-forecasting/3B6A9053C5872709A11F773E229F097C |journal=Annals of Actuarial Science |language=en |volume=11 |issue=2 |pages=343–389 |doi=10.1017/S1748499517000069 |issn=1748-4995|arxiv=1605.09484 }}</ref> This is consistent with the [[cohort effect]]s<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fung |first1=Man Chung |last2=Peters |first2=Gareth W. |last3=Shevchenko |first3=Pavel V. |date=2019 |title=Cohort effects in mortality modelling: a Bayesian state-space approach |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/annals-of-actuarial-science/article/abs/cohort-effects-in-mortality-modelling-a-bayesian-statespace-approach/E7C8C7910E754E8165F877194CD68FCF |journal=Annals of Actuarial Science |language=en |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=109–144 |doi=10.1017/S1748499518000131 |issn=1748-4995|arxiv=1703.08282 }}</ref> widely documented<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Holford |first=T R |date=1991 |title=Understanding the Effects of Age, Period, and Cohort on Incidence and Mortality Rates |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev.pu.12.050191.002233 |journal=Annual Review of Public Health |language=en |volume=12 |issue=1 |pages=425–457 |doi=10.1146/annurev.pu.12.050191.002233 |pmid=2049144 |issn=0163-7525|url-access=subscription }}</ref> in mortality observations.

His research work has been cited by the [[Swiss Association of Actuaries]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Gareth Peters to deliver keynote presentation at 108th AGM of Swiss Association of Actuaries |url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/statistics/news/news-210817 |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=University College London |date=21 August 2017 |language=en}}</ref> and informed [[central bank]] senior delegates around the world.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Gareth Peters invited keynote presenter at central banking conference in Abu Dhabi |url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/statistics/news/peters-conference-operational-risk-insurance |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=University College London|date=23 November 2017 |language=en}}</ref>
